items.stem: Claude Code keeps running the wrong test command in a repo. What is the most durable fix?

options.text: Record the correct test command in CLAUDE.md so it is applied every session
options.rationale: Correct: encoding the command in project context stops the repeated correction.

options.text: Re-type the correct command every time it is wrong
options.rationale: Repeating yourself does not persist the rule across sessions.

options.text: Delete the test suite so there is nothing to run
options.rationale: Removing tests is harmful and does not address the instruction.
The repo name does not determine the test command.

items.explanation: Correct: encoding the command in project context stops the repeated correction.

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a well-written CLAUDE.md? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The exact commands to build, test and lint the project
options.rationale: Correct: concrete commands let Claude Code act correctly without guessing.

options.text: Concrete conventions and do-nots specific to the repo
options.rationale: Correct: testable conventions reduce repeated corrections.

options.text: A copy of the entire source tree
options.rationale: The source tree is already available; duplicating it is noise.

options.text: Secrets such as API keys and passwords
options.rationale: Secrets must never be placed in project context files.

items.explanation: Correct: concrete commands let Claude Code act correctly without guessing.

items.stem: A monorepo's web package uses a different import style from the rest. Where should that rule live?

options.text: In a CLAUDE.md scoped to the web package directory
options.rationale: Correct: directory-scoped context applies the rule only where it is relevant.

options.text: In the root CLAUDE.md so it applies everywhere
options.rationale: Root scope would wrongly impose the web style on other packages.

options.text: In a code comment in one file
options.rationale: A single comment does not reliably steer Claude Code across the package.

options.text: Nowhere; the style should be abandoned
options.rationale: The package has a valid reason for its style; scope the rule instead.

items.explanation: Correct: directory-scoped context applies the rule only where it is relevant.
